Angular stylised 3D animation, brush-stroke texture, Horsell, Surrey, 1894, low sun from the left, black shadows.
[Shot 1] From 00:00 to 00:05. The shot opens on a wide of the open heather in the level sunset light: <Subject 1> in the grey herringbone tweed suit and the straw boater with a black band, his dark moustache neat walking away from the camera in a long curve through the knee-deep heather, his boater pushed back, a dark knot of standing people small at the left toward Woking and a second knot at the right toward Chobham, the ring of sand between them with the thin mast standing above it. The camera is on the heather three long strides behind him at a standing man's eye, a 35mm lens. The low sun comes from the LEFT. At the first frame the Narrator walks at the LEFT third of the frame, his back to the camera, from his straw boater at the TOP third to the heather at the BOTTOM edge. The shot is inside this place: Horsell Common with the sun going down in 1894: knee-deep purple-brown heather and dark furze running back from the camera, two young Scots pines standing clear of it. The camera tracks behind <Subject 1> at a walking pace with large amplitude, coming round with the curve of his track until the ring of sand stands at the centre of the picture, travelling four long strides as he swings his weight from one boot to the other through the heather, his head turned out to the sand all the way, from 00:00 to 00:02. At 00:02 the furze drags at his trouser leg and his right arm comes up across his chest, and the movement continues to the last frame of the shot. By 00:05 the camera is tracking through the last frame, and the action continues with it.
